clue.text: In which relaxation entails a certain amount of suspense?

definitions.text: In which relaxation entails a certain amount of suspense?

blocks.clueFragment: In which relaxation entails a certain amount of suspense?
blocks.note: surface reading: a tense, thrilling way to unwind, like a gripping novel
setter's reading: suspense means being literally hung up between two points while you rest

explanation.walkthrough: Suspense here is physical hanging, not dramatic tension: the bed is slung between two supports.
explanation.definitionFit: A swinging bed of netting or canvas, slung between posts or trees, used for lounging or sleeping.

clue.text: One thought of as lucky to be attractive?

definitions.text: One thought of as lucky to be attractive?

blocks.clueFragment: One thought of as lucky to be attractive?
blocks.note: surface reading: a fortunate person who happens to be good-looking
setter's reading: attractive in the physical sense of pulling iron, applied to a traditional good-luck charm

explanation.walkthrough: A horseshoe is the classic lucky charm; the U-shaped bar of iron that draws metal is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped permanent bar that draws iron, named after the shape of a traditional good-luck charm nailed above doors.

clue.text: Mucks about with old parts, primarily to construct models

indicators.note: to muck about is to mess around, so the letters are jumbled out of their given order
primarily points to the first letter, the one that comes before all the rest of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old
first letter of parts

explanation.surface: A modeller fiddles about with old components to build scale models.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock-ups are full-scale or rough working replicas built to test a design, so they are a kind of model.

clue.text: Monster turning up in Invergordon

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top
in says the letters sit inside a longer word of the clue

blocks.note: the middle letters of this Scottish town's name

explanation.surface: A monster sighting in the Highland town of Invergordon, a fitting tale for a Scottish paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Invergordon is a town on the Cromarty Firth in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy-tale giant that eats people is the classic monster of folklore.

clue.text: Weasel with mess of yolk covering skin, maybe

indicators.note: a mess is a disordered state, so the letters of the next word are jumbled
covering means wrapping around, so one set of letters goes outside the other
maybe hints that the word before it is only one possible arrangement of its letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weasel has made a mess of an egg yolk that has spilled over its skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are rearranged, with the jumbled yolk wrapped round the jumbled skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The kolinsky is a Siberian mink-like animal of the weasel family, prized for the fur used in fine paintbrushes.

clue.text: Dollars a wife's given for cutting tool

blocks.note: bucks is slang for dollars
taken as written
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone hands over dollars to buy a wife a saw.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucksaw is a saw with a blade set in an H-shaped wooden frame, used for cutting logs.

clue.text: Primate granting bishop a favour?

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
taken as written
a boon is a favour or blessing

explanation.surface: An archbishop, a Church primate, does a favour for a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: Primate looks ecclesiastical next to bishop, since an archbishop is a primate, but it is the monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A baboon is a large ground-dwelling African monkey, and monkeys belong to the primate order of mammals.

clue.text: Heraldic feature curiously lacking front, back and collar?

blocks.note: plain reading: a design on a shield

blocks.clueFragment: curiously lacking front, back and collar?
blocks.note: setter's reading: take a garment, remove its front, back and collar, and only its sleeves remain

explanation.walkthrough: Strip a jacket of front, back and collar and what is left is the sleeves, the parts for the limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The shield of emblems granted to a family or institution is the central device of heraldry.

clue.text: Diets I'm arranging, though subject to obstruction

indicators.note: arranging means putting things into a new order, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A dieter keeps planning meal regimes but is blocked at every turn.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an old variant spelling of stymied, from the golf term stymie.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stymied is to be blocked or thwarted, originally a golf ball in the way of another on the green.

clue.text: Means of improving dirty habits automatically

definitions.text: Means of improving dirty habits automatically

blocks.note: surface reading: a cure for bad personal behaviour
setter's reading: habits as garments, cleaned by an appliance

explanation.walkthrough: A habit is also a garment, as worn by a monk or nun, so dirty habits are soiled clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Household appliances that clean clothes by machine, laundering soiled garments without hand scrubbing.

clue.text: Volume of sound issued by such places?

definitions.text: Volume of sound issued by such places?

blocks.note: surface reading: loudness, as if these places were noisy
setter's reading: a volume is an item lent out, here one carrying audio rather than print

explanation.walkthrough: Volume suggests loudness, but here it is a lendable item, and the places lend discs instead of books.
explanation.definitionFit: Collections that lend out discs and tapes of music to members, as a book lending service does with novels.

clue.text: Birds American uncle decapitated

indicators.note: decapitated means the head is cut off, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: Uncle Remus is the narrator of Joel Chandler Harris's American folk tales

explanation.surface: Someone's uncle in America has beheaded a few birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Large flightless Australian runners, the second tallest living species after the ostrich.

clue.text: The year identified by a Roman numeral for 500?

blocks.clueFragment: The year identified by a Roman numeral for 500?
blocks.note: surface reading: a date written with a single Roman numeral
setter's reading: read literally as the letter A followed by the numeral for five hundred, the familiar abbreviation for a calendar era

explanation.walkthrough: Five hundred in Roman numerals is D, so 'a' plus that numeral spells the usual two-letter abbreviation for the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'in the year of the Lord', the phrase used to mark dates of the Christian era.

clue.text: Ornamental receptacle put together from cartons men unpacked

indicators.note: things unpacked are taken out and spread around, so these letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Workers unpack boxes and assemble a decorative container from the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic worship, an ornate vessel of gold or silver in which the consecrated Host is displayed.

clue.text: Is not without footwear or kneeling cushions

blocks.note: to not be without something is to have it
socks are worn on the feet

explanation.surface: A question of whether someone is wearing socks, or is kneeling on cushions in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm padded cushions found in church pews, used to kneel on during prayer.

clue.text: Friend turns round to follow poodle

indicators.note: turning round faces the other way, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: A friend turns around to see a poodle trailing after them.
explanation.walkthrough: Poodle is also used for a servile follower, which a lap-dog is too, but here it is simply the small pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pampered pet dog of the sort kept on one's knee, of which a toy poodle is an example.

clue.text: Lead uneventful existence, with no more credit?

blocks.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick
something over is finished, no more

explanation.surface: Someone lives a dull life now their credit has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay pieces appear in reverse of their clue order: credit first, then the word for finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that ticks over is idling, so a life ticking over is just carrying on quietly without much happening.

clue.text: Courageous sergeant's about to reveal way out

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters run backwards
to reveal says the letters are already present in the clue, waiting to be uncovered

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A brave sergeant is about to show his troops the escape route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' signals the backwards reading and 'to reveal' the concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: Egress is a formal word for an exit, the act or means of going out of a place.

clue.text: Royal train?

blocks.note: surface reading: the special railway carriages the monarch travels in
setter's reading: train as a body of attendants following an important person

explanation.walkthrough: A train is also the procession of followers behind a dignitary, not only a locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of aides and attendants who accompany a monarch or other important person.

clue.text: Drink, vermouth, knocked back by American before song

indicators.note: knocked back means sent backwards, so this word is read in reverse

blocks.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it
A is a standard abbreviation for American
Maria is a famous song from West Side Story

explanation.surface: An American downs a vermouth before singing a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking, apt next to vermouth, but it reverses the word for vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a brand of coffee liqueur from Jamaica, a drink served after dinner.

clue.text: Part of rigging made from broken trenail

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the pieces are put back together differently

blocks.note: a trenail is a wooden peg used in shipbuilding, taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of a ship's rigging fashioned from a broken wooden peg.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines are the small ropes tied across a ship's shrouds to form rungs for climbing aloft.

clue.text: Ready for holiday in Spain?

blocks.note: surface reading: a question of whether someone is packed and prepared to fly to Spain
setter's reading: ready as a noun, informal for cash, the money a traveller to Spain would have needed

explanation.walkthrough: The ready, or readies, is British slang for cash. Spain used this currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The former basic unit of Spanish currency, the cash a tourist would spend there before 2002.

clue.text: Ark defects unfortunately evident in areas near stern?

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters end up in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Noah's Ark shows its faults at the back of the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The deck areas toward the back of a ship, aft of the bridge or midships.

clue.text: Irritation with Italian church

blocks.note: It is a common abbreviation for Italian
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed with an Italian church.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a tickling skin sensation that prompts scratching, and by extension any nagging annoyance.

clue.text: Cut small cakes up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: buns are small cakes

explanation.surface: Someone slices small cakes into pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like an instruction to slice the cakes, but it means to ignore someone pointedly.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to ignore them deliberately, and a snub is exactly that kind of rebuff.

clue.text: Being not exactly intent on environs, managed to implement neutral policy

indicators.note: not exactly means not in precisely the given form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, except that its final S has no place in the answer

explanation.surface: A state too focused on its own surroundings adopts a policy of staying out of others' affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder has one letter too many: the S of environs is left over, so as printed the clue cannot work exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: A state's policy of not interfering in other countries' disputes or affairs is one of neutrality.

clue.text: Girl yonder, with sex appeal

blocks.note: yonder means over there
SA is the abbreviation for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A seductive young woman standing over there.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is a female given name, and crosswords use 'girl' for any woman's first name.

clue.text: They're habitually taking things the wrong way

definitions.text: They're habitually taking things the wrong way

blocks.clueFragment: They're habitually taking things the wrong way
blocks.note: surface reading: touchy people who always misinterpret what is said
setter's reading: taking other people's property by unlawful means, as a matter of routine

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking things the wrong way' sounds like being easily offended, but read literally it is stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves who steal from people or premises, often by force, make a habit of illegal taking.
